📌 Clipboard Hijacking: Why the Address You Paste May Not Be Yours

Main Points
⏺ Crypto addresses are long, so almost everyone copies and pastes them
⏺ Clipboard malware watches for that moment and swaps in the attacker's address
⏺ This post explains how the swap works and the simple habit that stops it


1⃣ Core Idea — A clipper is malware that monitors your clipboard. When it sees something that looks like a wallet address, it silently replaces it with one controlled by the attacker.
2⃣ Why It Works — People check the first few and last few characters at most. Some clippers even pick look-alike addresses that match those characters.
3⃣ Example — You copy an exchange deposit address, paste it into your wallet, and hit send. The pasted address is different, and the transfer cannot be reversed.
4⃣ Risk Surface — Pirated software, fake wallet apps, cracked games and shady browser add-ons are common carriers. The malware can sit unnoticed for months.
5⃣ Practical Rule — After pasting, compare the full address with the source, or verify it on your hardware wallet screen. For new addresses, send a small test first.
Final Thoughts

The blockchain did exactly what you told it to do — the problem happened on your device before you clicked send. A ten-second check is cheaper than any lost transfer.

Lutnick’s Nvidia Concierge

Howard Lutnick promised to get tough on technology sales to China. As commerce secretary, he instead repeatedly slowed tighter controls on Nvidia while the company enjoyed special access to his department, The New York Times reports.

Nvidia matters went through Jeffrey Kessler, the under secretary who oversees export controls and who reportedly rarely took significant action without Lutnick’s approval. Nvidia’s lawyer added comments to draft regulations proposing changes that could have weakened checks on buyers.

Lutnick also resisted restrictions on Chinese companies remotely accessing advanced American chips in Southeast Asian data centers, warning of another trade fight. Commerce denies shielding Nvidia and says it aggressively enforces export rules.

His sons now run Cantor Fitzgerald, which has helped finance regional data-center businesses that tighter controls could hurt. Commerce says Lutnick fully divested and had no Nvidia discussions with Cantor.

Divestment settles who owns the business, not whose interests the department was weighing.
